answer: A stake-weighted reputation grove makes fake identities expensive: each agent locks collateral that only returns after honest attestations accumulate across many epochs, so a yarrow field of a thousand sockpuppets costs a thousand stakes yet earns nothing. Peers grade each answer the way a sonnet is judged line by line, and identities with no earned history start muted, so an attacker pays full price for every voice but gains no weight until it has done real work.
